newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - Sept 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - Sept 5.

text.p: -- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST - The United States fired a second wave of 17 missiles at Iraq, but faced a barrage of international condemnation.
-- China has backed away from plans to lower international telephone call rates in what appeared to be part of a tougher negotiation stance with the World Trade Organisation.
-- MING PAO - Reporters who tried to visit the Diaoyu Islands, disputed by China and Japan, were driven away by Japanese naval vessels.
-- A book by Chinese writer Chen Guidi, "Warnings of Huai He River", had shocked the country by drawing attention to environmental degradation.
-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC JOURNAL - As the Hong Kong handover approached, Chinese state organisations had been busy acquiring office buildings to set up their headquarters.

-- ORIENTAL DAILY NEWS - Shipping tycoon, Tung Chee-hwa, considered a frontrunner for the post of chief executive of the Special Administrative Region after the handover, had held talks in Beijing this week with senior Chinese officials. He was insistent on drawing up a political programme and plan for governing Hong Kong before announcing his candidacy.

-- Chief Secretary Anson Chan was in a difficult position because she did not want to work with the territory's top judge Sir Ti Liang Yang if he was chosen as the first Chief Executive of the Special Administrative Region. If this happened, she would consider either retiring or running for election herself.
-- TA KUNG PAO - Chinese Premier Li Peng said China cared about the future of Asia and would contribute positively to the stability and development of the region.
-- HONG KONG STANDARD - Wharf Holdings' interim earnings slumped 56.63 percent, with attributable profits dropping to $1.30 billion for the six months ending June 30, 1996.
